timing: Durable ClientResult.started_at/completed_at, cross-checked against immutable entrypoint log ordering and fixed native benchmark rates for all 20 reported allocations. Client intervals include pipeline fill, drain and output work after serving startup.
cost: Actual Slurm GPU count times actual array-task elapsed seconds / 3600, including all attempts, startup and shutdown. Array-parent summaries are not double counted. Comparison rows exclude smoke allocations; complete new-experiment accounting is also summarized here. GPU-hours are not full monetary cost.
validation: Post-generation schema validation is separate from this performance comparison. Historical validation audit evidence remains preserved privately.
limitations: Each sweep point is one trial. One separately named one-node C1024 confirmation per TP4/TP8 is reported separately, without confidence intervals. The one-node TP8 repeat was faster than its sweep point and came within 1% of the two-node TP8 sweep point; a reliable two-node throughput advantage is not established. No absolute hardware maximum, fleet-scale throughput, production generation, or interrupted-generation recovery test was measured.
projection_note: Untested projections for one million generated records use the original sweep generated-record rate times (14400 - measured pre-client seconds - ceil(post-client seconds)). Jobs and four-hour waves round up. Four allocation slots reserve 32 GPUs for one-node jobs or 64 GPUs for two-node jobs. A fixed 32-GPU budget permits four one-node or two two-node jobs. Queue wait, extra safety margin, failures, final collection and fleet scaling variability are excluded.
historical_cohort: Earlier cohorts used max_num_seqs=128 per replica; older released-runtime trials also had a 256-connection proxy cap or a smaller client window. All remain separate and are excluded from this cohort and its frontier.
telemetry: Five-second per-GPU and per-replica samples; ten-second client progress. Token rates use counter deltas. Backend request histograms include server queues and describe completing requests, not full pipeline latency. Both full-client and central60% descriptive windows were checked; central windows do not establish steady state. Proxy diagnostic counts are the last observed counters within each client interval.

runtime_source.status: Isolated experimental build based on release 1.0.0 with only the linked timing and proxy net changes. All other source hashes and dependency versions held fixed; this is historical experimental provenance, not an assertion about a shipped release.

client_concurrency_semantics: Configured per-alias concurrency ceilings, shared across all five model columns. Queue-admission HTTP 429s can trigger client AIMD backoff and deferred retries; the ceiling is not a constant achieved concurrency.

extension_rule.matching_rule: A two-node doubled concurrency may be measured to match a healthy measured one-node extension.
extension_rule.reason: One-node TP8 improved from C512 to C1024, qualifying C2048; its decline stopped C4096. Two-node C4096 matched the healthy one-node C2048 observation; its decline stopped C8192. Highest tested limits are not hardware maxima.
extension_rule.scope_note: Historical run-extension criteria are preserved as executed; schema validation is not the reported performance metric.

completion_time_projection.method: Estimated generation hours = ceil(total_jobs / max_concurrent_jobs) * hours_per_job. Peak GPUs = max_concurrent_jobs * gpus_per_job. Job counts use generated throughput, measured startup and rounded-up shutdown. Each array task is one job. Full-wave budgets can overestimate a shorter final wave.
completion_time_projection.limitations: Untested fleet projections from single-client trials. Assumes generated throughput persists over four-hour jobs and parallel allocations. Excludes queue wait, extra safety margin, failures and final collection time. Measured cases used at most 16 GPUs in one allocation.
completion_time_projection.rate_basis: Original observed sweep frontiers; planned confirmations are listed separately. Four-hour-wave estimates show a tie at four slots despite using different GPU budgets.

comparison_scope: One 16-CPU client and one proxy per allocation. Compare TP4/TP8 single-client concurrency sweeps on one and two nodes; each projected production job repeats one selected single-client setting.

confirmation_interpretation.selection_basis: Original sweep observations select concurrency. Confirmations remain separate; projections use original sweep rates.

new_tp8_experiment_all_attempt_accountin.scope: TP8 smoke, ten TP8 sweep cases and the two planned one-node TP4/TP8 confirmations; earlier TP4 cohort accounting remains separate.

throughput_metric: All generated output records (schema-valid plus schema-invalid) divided by full durable client runtime. Schema validation does not filter performance rates, GPU cost, or target-record projections.
